title: JavaScript APIs and Fetch Applied Check
description: Test your ability to build fetch requests, handle status codes and JSON, use headers and query params, and diagnose common CORS issues.
author: DailyCoder

options.text: `response.json()` returns a Promise and should be awaited

questions.explanation: `response.json()` is asynchronous. Without `await`, `data` is a Promise.

questions.prompt: Which code correctly treats HTTP error statuses as errors?

options.text: `const response = await fetch(url); if (!response.ok) throw new Error(String(response.status));`
`const response = await fetch(url); if (response.ok) throw new Error();`

questions.explanation: `fetch` does not reject for HTTP statuses like 404, so checking `response.ok` is important.

questions.prompt: Which request correctly sends JSON to create a user?
questions.explanation: A JSON POST request should set the method, content type header, and stringified JSON body.

questions.prompt: What should you be careful about with a `204 No Content` response?

options.text: It may not have a body, so calling `response.json()` can fail
It always means the request failed
It always contains a large JSON body
It is a CORS-only status code

questions.explanation: `204 No Content` means there is no response body to parse.

questions.prompt:
What is the origin difference here?
```text
http://localhost:3000
http://localhost:5000
```

options.text: They are different origins because the ports differ
They are the same origin because both use localhost
They are same-origin only for POST requests

questions.explanation: Origin includes protocol, domain, and port. Different ports mean different origins.

questions.prompt: Why is `mode: "no-cors"` usually not a real fix for API calls?

options.text: It produces an opaque response that JavaScript cannot read normally
It disables all browser security permanently

questions.explanation: `no-cors` does not let normal frontend code read the response body/status like a standard API response.

questions.prompt:
Which is the best way to build this search URL safely?
```text
/api/search?q=javascript basics
```

options.text: `const params = new URLSearchParams({ q: "javascript basics" }); fetch(`/api/search?${params}`);`
`fetch("/api/search?q=" + "javascript basics")` always safely handles all input

questions.prompt: Which Authorization header is commonly expected for bearer-token APIs?
questions.explanation: Many APIs expect the `Bearer` prefix in the `Authorization` header.

questions.prompt: What is a likely problem with hard-coding a secret API key in frontend JavaScript?

options.text: Frontend source code is visible to users, so the secret can be exposed
API keys only work in CSS
Hard-coded strings always cause syntax errors

questions.explanation: Secrets should not be placed in public frontend code. Use a backend for secret-protected API calls.

questions.prompt: Which method is best for updating only part of a resource?
questions.explanation: `PATCH` is commonly used for partial updates.

options.text: Includes credentials such as cookies in cross-origin requests too
Automatically adds a bearer token from nowhere

questions.explanation: `credentials: "include"` tells fetch to include credentials even for cross-origin requests, subject to CORS rules.

questions.prompt: What CORS header usually tells the browser which frontend origin may read the response?
questions.explanation: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` is the key CORS response header for allowed origins.

options.text: An automatic browser `OPTIONS` request sent before certain cross-origin requests
A request that always avoids CORS

questions.explanation: Browsers send preflight `OPTIONS` requests for certain cross-origin requests to check server permission.

questions.prompt: Which statement about CORS is correct?

options.text: CORS controls whether browser JavaScript can read cross-origin responses
CORS prevents all servers from receiving requests
CORS is fixed by changing `await` to `.then()`

questions.explanation: CORS is a browser security feature controlling cross-origin response access.

questions.prompt: Which approach is often useful during local frontend/backend development to avoid CORS friction?

options.text: A development proxy that forwards `/api` requests to the backend
Hard-coding all API secrets in the browser

questions.explanation: A dev proxy can make API requests appear same-origin to the browser during local development.
